checks: Checked 19899b61b9ca5f3a §§1–2, (1)–(7). At each height, the three chosen horizontal normals have vertex values (2r,−r,−r), so the isolated-vertex cap area is (2r+β(t−t_0)−c)²/2 when proper. Direct integration gives V=9A, the raw polynomial and the two moment integrals. Independent exact rational polynomial evaluations agree.

The smaller quadratic root rationalizes to (Aβ²/3)/(2−βt_0+sqrt(4−4βt_0−β²/3)). The denominator exceeds three even on ε≤1/2, |β|≤1/8, and A≤13/12. The resulting bound gives |c_β−β(t−t_0)|<1/2≤r, verifying the proper slice status. The raw derivative is negative at that root; local strict decrease and global nonincrease imply uniqueness at that mass.

A point violating a quantile inequality lies in a slightly tightened closed cap of mass strictly less than Q. Averaging the three constraints and taking both signs of β to zero forces the vertical displacement to vanish, and β=0 then forces zero horizontal displacement. This is an inclusion of the depth region, without claiming its nonemptiness from the three chosen normals.

The positive weights give the exact vertical resultant for either sign of tilt. Normalization by individual lengths preserves weighted thresholds after multiplying the coefficients by those lengths. Projection on the vertical axis gives the lower bound on total weight; the leading threshold factor is A/12 and the raw cap excess/slack ratio is S_0=4.

overlap.comparison: General paired centroid tails can support a separate all-normal argument, but do not yield the frustum quantile roots, coarea or limiting positive coefficients. The present proof uses only the specified cap directions.

readability: Q is a specified raw level here. The implication for points of depth at least Q does not assert that Y attains Q over all normals.

summary: The near-quantile roots, coarea and reciprocal normal recovery are exact in the specified small-tilt regime. The draft avoids an unproved all-normal equality claim.
